prompt:
The times, $t$ minutes, that 60 students took to complete a task are shown.

| Time | $0<t\le10$ | $10<t\le20$ | $20<t\le30$ | $30<t\le40$ | $40<t\le50$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 6 | 14 | 22 | 12 | 6 |

**(a)** Write down the cumulative frequencies. **[1]**

**(b)** Using a cumulative frequency graph (or linear interpolation), estimate the median and the interquartile range. **[3]**

**(c)** Estimate the number of students who took more than 35 minutes. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $6,\ 20,\ 42,\ 54,\ 60$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Median at the 30th student: $20+\dfrac{30-20}{22}\times10\approx24.5$ min **(A1)**

$Q_1$ (15th): $10+\dfrac{9}{14}\times10\approx16.4$; $Q_3$ (45th): $30+\dfrac{3}{12}\times10=32.5$ **(M1)**; IQR $\approx16$ min **(A1)**

**(c)** At $t=35$, cumulative frequency $\approx42+6=48$, so about $60-48=12$ students **(A1)**

Answers read from a hand-drawn graph within about ±1 min are acceptable.

prompt:
State an appropriate diagram for each data set and give a reason:

**(a)** the number of siblings of 40 students; **(b)** the heights of 40 students.
markscheme:
**(a)** Discrete: a frequency table or bar chart (vertical line graph) with a bar for each value **(A1)**

**(b)** Continuous: a grouped frequency table with a histogram (bars touching), or a cumulative frequency graph **(A1)**

prompt: The number of goals scored in 12 matches were: $0,2,1,1,3,0,2,1,4,1,0,2$. Construct a frequency table and use it to find the total number of goals.

The times, $t$ minutes, that 60 students took to complete a task are shown.

| Time | $0<t\le10$ | $10<t\le20$ | $20<t\le30$ | $30<t\le40$ | $40<t\le50$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 6 | 14 | 22 | 12 | 6 |

Describe the shape of the histogram for these data and explain why the bars touch.
markscheme: Roughly symmetric and single-peaked, centred on the $20$–$30$ class **(A1)**. Time is continuous, so the classes have no gaps between them **(R1)**

prompt:
A data set has minimum 3, $Q_1=8$, median 11, $Q_3=15$ and maximum 30. The second largest value is 22.

**(a)** Show that 30 is an outlier. **[1]**

**(b)** Describe how the box and whisker diagram should be drawn. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $15+1.5(15-8)=25.5<30$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Box from 8 to 15 with a line at 11 **(A1)**; lower whisker to 3, upper whisker to 22 (largest non-outlier), and 30 marked as a separate cross **(A1)**
